editorial:
Imagine stepping into a machine that lets you relive your old memories like a movie. That is exactly what happens here when a therapist uses high-tech virtual reality to help a young man get over a nasty breakup. You get to see these digital memories play out, but as you watch, you start to notice that things aren't adding up. The vibe is tense and mysterious, making you feel like you are solving a puzzle alongside the doctor. It is a cool take on how our brains can trick us into remembering things that never actually happened.

The acting is solid and keeps you locked into the story, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. The big twists are what really make it work, as they completely change how you see the characters. If you enjoy mind-bending stories, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: You find out that the memories were not accurate because the young man was actually the toxic one in the relationship. He used the VR technology to rewrite his history and make himself look like the victim. The twist reveals that he manipulated the therapist and the machine to hide his own crimes. In the end, the truth comes out, showing that his mind created a fake version of events to escape guilt.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and tech-based thrillers.
